candidates.name: Per-descriptor close-on-exec control with fcntl
candidates.reason: Setting the close-on-exec flag on unwanted descriptors lets the operating system remove them at program execution regardless of which higher-level launcher reaches that execution boundary.
candidates.application_scope: A descriptor-level inheritance policy across standard-library and extension-module execution paths, while treating standard input/output/error (0, 1, 2) and explicitly passed additional descriptors separately.
candidates.constraints_or_caveat: A separate flag-setting call leaves a creation-to-flag interval in concurrent programs; a policy must cover every creation and duplication path, and close-on-exec does not itself prevent the initial fork from copying descriptors.
candidates.date_evidence: The opened archived Apple fcntl manual has a 1994-01-12 footer and documents F_GETFD/F_SETFD; the opened posix_spawn manual dated 2007-08-09 independently confirms the close-on-exec exception across spawning.

candidates.name: Atomic close-on-exec file creation with open/openat O_CLOEXEC
candidates.reason: Passing O_CLOEXEC when opening a file removes the race in which another thread executes a child between descriptor creation and a later fcntl call.
candidates.application_scope: Regular-file and directory descriptor acquisition in a common runtime layer and cooperating native modules.
candidates.constraints_or_caveat: Requires platform support and coverage at each acquisition site; it does not retrofit already-open descriptors, and intended inheritance needs an explicit exception.
candidates.date_evidence: Opened Linux man-pages 6.19 page dated 2026-02-08, rendered 2026-09-09; it says O_CLOEXEC was introduced in Linux 2.6.23, but no contemporaneous pre-cutoff source was opened, so this evidence is retained as later.

candidates.name: Close-on-exec pipe creation with pipe2
candidates.reason: pipe2 with O_CLOEXEC marks both pipe endpoints during creation so auxiliary communication pipes do not remain open in an unrelated executed program.
candidates.application_scope: Pipes created by process wrappers, runtime internals and native modules.
candidates.constraints_or_caveat: Both endpoints must be considered, and an endpoint intentionally mapped to a child's standard stream must be retained explicitly; unsupported platforms need a different implementation.
candidates.date_evidence: Opened Linux man-pages 6.19 page dated 2026-02-08 and rendered 2026-09-09; no pre-cutoff edition was retrieved.

candidates.name: Close-on-exec socket creation with SOCK_CLOEXEC
candidates.reason: Adding SOCK_CLOEXEC to socket creation gives networking modules the same execution-boundary inheritance control as file-opening code.
candidates.application_scope: New socket descriptors opened by the runtime or cooperating networking extensions.
candidates.constraints_or_caveat: This covers descriptors created by socket(), not every later socket-producing operation; platform capability checks and intentional descriptor-passing behavior still need a defined policy.
candidates.date_evidence: Opened Linux man-pages 6.19 socket page dated 2025-10-29 and rendered 2026-09-09; its Linux 2.6.27 introduction statement was not treated as a retrieved pre-cutoff edition.

candidates.name: Close-on-exec descriptor duplication with dup3
candidates.reason: dup3 with O_CLOEXEC prevents duplication from silently reintroducing an inheritable descriptor after its original descriptor was protected.
candidates.application_scope: Descriptor copies and remapping performed by low-level runtime or extension code.
candidates.constraints_or_caveat: Ordinary dup/dup2 clear the flag on a new duplicate, so callers cannot assume it is shared with the original; intended standard-stream remapping has different inheritance requirements, and dup3 rejects equal source and destination numbers.
candidates.date_evidence: Opened Linux man-pages 6.19 page dated 2026-02-08 and rendered 2026-09-09; it identifies Linux 2.6.27/glibc 2.9 for dup3, but no contemporaneous dated implementation was opened.

candidates.name: Ordered descriptor actions with posix_spawn
candidates.reason: An ordered spawn file-actions object provides a concrete way to declare child-specific descriptor changes while unmodified close-on-exec descriptors are closed.
candidates.application_scope: A complementary launch-time contract for opening, closing or remapping descriptors and preserving deliberately configured standard streams.
candidates.constraints_or_caveat: This only governs launch paths that use the configured spawn call, so it complements descriptor-level flags and cannot by itself protect other launchers or arbitrary external modules.
candidates.date_evidence: Opened archived Apple posix_spawn manual dated 2007-08-09 and file-actions manual dated 2007-08-22, both before the 2013-08-28 cutoff.

raw_response:
## C11 — catalogue baseline B

I found six useful mechanisms. My design inference is to put inheritance control at descriptor acquisition and duplication, then preserve standard input, output and error (descriptors 0, 1 and 2) and any explicitly passed extra descriptors according to an explicit contract. This can cover multiple execution entry points when the descriptor-producing code participates; a launch-specific cleanup option alone cannot cover unrelated launchers.

All six were discovered in the opened [Awesome System Calls catalogue](https://github.com/edigaryev/awesome-system-calls). The primary documentation was opened only after that discovery.

1. **Per-descriptor close-on-exec control with fcntl.** Setting the close-on-exec flag on unwanted descriptors lets the operating system remove them at program execution regardless of which higher-level launcher reaches that execution boundary. The archived [fcntl manual](https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/System/Conceptual/ManPages_iPhoneOS/man2/fcntl.2.html) documents F_GETFD/F_SETFD, and the archived [posix_spawn manual](https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/System/Conceptual/ManPages_iPhoneOS/man2/posix_spawn.2.html) confirms the same exception during spawning. The flag applies at execution, not at the initial fork; creation and duplication paths still need coverage. **Date evidence: pre-decision**, with manual footers dated 1994-01-12 and 2007-08-09.

2. **Atomic close-on-exec file creation with open/openat O_CLOEXEC.** Passing O_CLOEXEC when opening a file removes the race in which another thread executes a child between descriptor creation and a later fcntl call. The [open manual](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/open.2.html) explicitly explains this race. This is useful for file and directory acquisition in a common runtime layer, subject to platform support and explicit exceptions for intended inheritance. **Date evidence: post-decision**; the opened edition is dated 2026-02-08, although it reports introduction in Linux 2.6.23.

3. **Close-on-exec pipe creation with pipe2.** pipe2 with O_CLOEXEC marks both pipe endpoints during creation so auxiliary communication pipes do not remain open in an unrelated executed program. The [pipe manual](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/pipe.2.html) confirms that both returned descriptors receive the flag. A deliberately passed endpoint, including one mapped to a child's standard stream, still needs explicit handling. **Date evidence: post-decision**; the opened edition is dated 2026-02-08.

4. **Close-on-exec socket creation with SOCK_CLOEXEC.** Adding SOCK_CLOEXEC to socket creation gives networking modules the same execution-boundary inheritance control as file-opening code. The [socket manual](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/socket.2.html) documents the creation flag. This covers socket() itself; a complete policy must also address other socket-producing operations and intentional passing. **Date evidence: post-decision**; the opened edition is dated 2025-10-29 and mentions Linux 2.6.27 as the introduction version.

5. **Close-on-exec descriptor duplication with dup3.** dup3 with O_CLOEXEC prevents duplication from silently reintroducing an inheritable descriptor after its original descriptor was protected. The [duplication manual](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/dup2.2.html) distinguishes ordinary duplication, which clears the new descriptor's flag, from dup3's explicit flag setting. Standard-stream remapping needs intentional inheritance semantics, and dup3 rejects identical source and destination descriptor numbers. **Date evidence: post-decision**; the opened edition is dated 2026-02-08 and identifies Linux 2.6.27/glibc 2.9.

6. **Ordered descriptor actions with posix_spawn.** An ordered spawn file-actions object provides a concrete way to declare child-specific descriptor changes while unmodified close-on-exec descriptors are closed. The archived [file-actions manual](https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/System/Conceptual/ManPages_iPhoneOS/man3/posix_spawn_file_actions_init.3.html) supplies this contract. It complements a descriptor-level policy, but applies only to launch paths that use the configured spawn call. **Date evidence: pre-decision**, with the file-actions manual dated 2007-08-22.

These are transfer candidates, not claims that a particular design deployed them or proved them useful. The current Linux manuals remain later evidence; their old-version references were not used to backdate the retrieved pages. This was an internal separate-context run by GPT-6 Astra Pro, not a human study. Model pretraining was not controlled, and a remembered topic association is recorded in the exposure log. The search used five exact catalogue-restricted queries and seventeen explicit page-open attempts, including four failures; in-page finds only revisited already-opened documents.
